summary: Iter59 Phase A (Driver Shortage Policy Engine) fully verified. All 10 pytest cases pass. Backend deploy-readiness endpoint returns exit_code=0, status=pass. Auth health OK. Verified via API: policy CRUD, resolve by trip_date, historical snapshot on trip CREATE (200KG cat 'TestUI59' produced correct DR block), snapshot preservation on trip UPDATE (added a newer 300KG policy — snapshot on the pre-existing trip remained locked to the original 200KG policy_id/version/allowed_limit_kg), manual override with reason writes override + audit and preserves system_recovery_amount, blank reason rejected with 422, clearing override reverts final=system and appends 'clear' entry to driver_recovery_history. Verified via UI: /login demo login → /dashboard renders with Save-Health tile (sparkline visible) + Deploy Guard tile showing 'Guard PASS · Safe to Deploy'. Sidebar shows nav-shortage-policies. /drivers/shortage-policies loads (policies-page + policies-table testids present). Created 'Standard 100KG UI' policy (v1 + Active). Edited limit to 120 → row now shows v2 (version bumped). Deactivate → row shows Inactive. Multi-company isolation not exhaustively tested in UI (only single company visible) but backend pytest 'test_multi_company_isolation' already validates it.

issues: Long unbounded scrolling list of pre-existing seed policies (HistNew_IT59_*, IsoIA_IT59_*, CRUD_IT59_*, OverrideTest_IT59_* etc.) makes it hard to find a newly-created policy — pagination / filter / search would improve usability.

critical_code_review_comments: trips.py update flow correctly preserves prev_snap and never re-resolves policy on update — audit-critical rule satisfied.

build_trip_driver_recovery_snapshot returns None if trip has no driver_id (silent). Consider snapshotting even for driver-less trips or documenting this behaviour so testers know shortage_qty alone won't trigger a snapshot.

shortage_qty on Trip is in MT but _compute_trip may auto-derive shortage_qty from loaded/unloaded quantities; when clients send an explicit shortage_qty=0.150 with tons=10 unloaded=0, the computed shortage becomes tons (10 MT = 10000 KG). Recommend documenting or accepting an explicit-mode flag so shortage isn't overwritten.
Policies list page renders all rows unpaginated — will degrade over time; add search/pagination.
test_credentials: Bearer test_session_bitumen_2026 (demo user). Login via data-testid=demo-login-button on /login.
seed_data_creation: Created via UI/API for verification: policies 'Standard 100KG UI' (v1→v2, deactivated), 'UITest100', 'UITest200', 'UITest300' (all product_category=TestUI59). Trip trip_46dcca369bc14c8c with driver_recovery snapshot for regression evidence.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase A driver shortage policy engine is stable. Historical snapshot is proven immutable across trip updates (verified with a newer 300KG policy in place — trip retained 200KG snapshot). Override + clear + audit history + blank-reason rejection all working. Deploy Guard passing (regression_guard.status=pass, exit_code=0). When retesting, remember: shortage_qty is stored in MT on Trip and multiplied by 1000 for KG comparison; build_trip_driver_recovery_snapshot requires driver_id — API callers without driver_id will get driver_recovery=null (by design). Phases B (Driver Trip History) and C (Salary/Payment Ledger) are deferred — do not test.
rca of the issue: No issues found. All acceptance criteria met.
